clue.text: Talk directly, given Spooner's sound of the fog horn?

indicators.note: Spooner's tells us to swap the opening sounds of two words, as the Reverend Spooner was said to do

parts.note: a foghorn's noise could be called a hoot from the ship, which gives the phrase to be swapped
the same phrase supplies its last word, the ship, as the second half of the swap

explanation.surface: Someone who speaks bluntly is compared, jokingly, to the blast of a ship's foghorn.
explanation.walkthrough: The foghorn's sound is a 'hoot from the ship'; swapping the H of hoot with the SH of ship gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To speak impulsively and frankly, without careful preparation, is an idiom borrowed from a gunslinger firing without aiming.

clue.text: Mimed to a T, cued badly

indicators.note: badly says the letters of the preceding words are put together wrongly, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: An actor performs a mime perfectly, though the prompts came in badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Badly' rearranges the eight letters of TO A T CUED.
explanation.definitionFit: Performing something with gestures rather than words is a synonym for miming it.

clue.text: Iffy novel about debasement ultimately, fiend from hell shackling female in vacuous story?

definitions.text: Iffy novel about debasement ultimately, fiend from hell shackling female in vacuous story?

indicators.note: about means going around, so the shuffled letters wrap the next piece
novel, meaning new or fresh, asks for the letters of the word before it to be made anew in another order
ultimately points to the final letter of the word debasement
in places the whole hellish sequence inside the emptied story
vacuous means empty, so the word story is emptied of everything but its outer letters
from says the fiend comes out of hell, so the fiend's letters follow hell's

parts.note: Hades is the underworld of Greek myth, hell

indicators.note: shackling means holding captive, so the fiend's letters enclose the next piece

parts.note: an ogre is a monster or fiend

explanation.surface: A sneering review of an erotic bestseller: a dodgy book about degradation, a devil holding a woman captive, an empty tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' (new) rearranges the opening word around T; 'shackling' sets F inside the fiend, which follows hell as 'from' says; 'in' puts it all within the ends of 'story', emptied by 'vacuous'.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole clue describes E L James's notorious bestselling erotic romance, a book about sexual submission that critics found thin.

clue.text: Scatter spiders spinning on middle of web

indicators.note: spinning, as spiders do with silk, here whirls the letters of spiders into a new order
middle of picks out the central letter of the word web

explanation.surface: Spiders scatter as they whirl around on their web.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spinning' rearranges SPIDERS; E, the middle of 'web', goes on the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To scatter things is to spread them widely in different directions, a direct synonym.

clue.text: See 3
See 16
A feature of a carnival on the sea

parts.note: a float is a decorated vehicle in a carnival parade

explanation.surface: A carnival float appears on the sea, perhaps at a seaside regatta.
explanation.definitionFit: Something drifting on the water's surface rather than sinking is described with this adjective.

clue.text: Grass reported a couple of cons in rhyme

indicators.note: reported means spoken, so we want a word that sounds like dried grass

parts.note: hay is dried grass

indicators.note: a couple of means two, so the word for cons is given twice

parts.note: to diddle someone is to con or swindle them

explanation.surface: An informer tells police about two swindles, set out in verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grass' reads as informer, but here it is dried grass, whose sound gives the opening exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: The words open a well-known English nursery rhyme about a cat and a fiddle.

clue.text: Hellish extremists welcoming old Communist leader, that man in Asian revolutionary

indicators.note: welcoming means taking in, so the outer letters hold the following pieces
extremists means the letters at the two extremes of the word Hellish
leader means the first letter of the word Communist

parts.note: him is the pronoun for that man
taken as written

explanation.surface: A hellish set of radicals welcomes an ex-Communist leader; that man is in an Asian revolution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremists' gives the two H's at the ends of 'Hellish', and 'welcoming' has them enclose everything else.
explanation.definitionFit: The Vietnamese communist leader who led the struggle for independence from France was a revolutionary from Asia.

clue.text: Upset about head of family one's butted?

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for upset surrounds the next letter

parts.note: to rile someone is to upset them

indicators.note: head of picks the first letter of the word family

explanation.surface: Someone is upset at being headbutted by the head of the family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butted' suggests headbutting; the definition means something that has a butt, as a gun does.
explanation.definitionFit: A gun of this kind has a wooden butt at the shoulder end, so it is playfully a thing that is butted.

clue.text: Dance round home with record

parts.note: a round shape is the letter O
a nest is a bird's home
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A dance is performed around the house with a record playing.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an early twentieth-century ballroom dance in quick march time.

clue.text: Matt finish in mind around one card

indicators.note: around means the first pieces wrap round the next

parts.note: Matt Damon is the American actor
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: finish in picks the final letter of the word mind

explanation.surface: A finish of matt paint is in mind, around one particular card.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Matt finish' reads as a dull paint coating; in fact Matt is the actor, and 'finish in mind' is D.
explanation.definitionFit: A playing card from the red suit marked with lozenge shapes is one of these.

clue.text: See 23
Tried describing some 12s in exercise with 12s

indicators.note: in puts the cut gems inside the exercise

parts.note: PE is physical education, exercise
12s refers to the answer to 12, so some diamonds are rose-cut ones, a style of cutting gems
in card games D abbreviates the suit of diamonds

explanation.surface: An attempt to describe certain gems within a workout, alongside more gems.
explanation.walkthrough: '12s' cross-refers to the answer at 12-across, DIAMOND. 'Describing' is a link word here.
explanation.definitionFit: A defendant who has been taken to court and tried has been charged and put through legal proceedings.

clue.text: Female writer capturing hearts with article, distorted

indicators.note: capturing means holding inside, so the female and writer pieces hold the next letters

parts.note: miss is the title of an unmarried female
a pen is something to write with
H abbreviates the card suit of hearts
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A woman writer captures hearts with a piece she has twisted out of shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Something deformed or out of its proper shape is a synonym for distorted.

clue.text: Recording away from the studio — tedious?

parts.note: the first word of the answer uses the same seven letters as tedious, and the second word, meaning scattered abroad, is read as the instruction to scatter them

explanation.surface: A programme recorded on location is dismissed as tedious.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as a piece of wordplay: its first word is TEDIOUS with its letters scattered, and its second word is the signal for that scattering.
explanation.definitionFit: A television or radio programme made on location rather than in a studio has this name in broadcasting.

clue.text: Profligate is no longer taking risks, enjoying life for starters

parts.note: was is the past of is, describing what no longer is

indicators.note: for starters picks the first letter of each of the four words before it

explanation.surface: A spendthrift has stopped taking risks and enjoying life.
explanation.definitionFit: A wasteful person who squanders money is a profligate, used here as a noun.

clue.text: Very exciting bit I can't hear, nothing trivial, initially

parts.note: a whit is a tiny bit
eh is what you say when you can't hear
nothing is zero, the letter O

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of the word trivial

explanation.surface: An exciting moment that I couldn't hear, nothing important at first.
explanation.definitionFit: Glowing at extreme temperature, the word also describes something intensely exciting or popular.

clue.text: Famous singer causes agitation to sailor

parts.note: to rock someone is to shake or agitate them
a tar is a sailor

explanation.surface: A celebrity vocalist upsets a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: A celebrated performer of popular guitar-driven music is often a famous singer.

clue.text: One waking up with buzz, going after first of tsetse flies

indicators.note: going after places the rouser and buzz pieces after that letter
first of picks the opening letter of the word tsetse

parts.note: a rouser is one who wakes people up
zip means energy or buzz

explanation.surface: Someone waking up to a buzzing sound, as tsetse flies follow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flies' looks like part of the insect picture but is the definition: the fastening on trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: The fastening on the front of a pair of trousers is known in Britain as the flies.

clue.text: See 3
Cut cherry, juicier with odd bits removed

parts.note: cherry is a shade of red

indicators.note: dropping the odd-numbered letters leaves the second, fourth and sixth letters of juicier

explanation.surface: Slicing a cherry, juicier once the odd bits are trimmed.
explanation.definitionFit: To lessen or diminish something is to cut it, as with costs.

clue.text: Drug treatment to get over cold

indicators.note: to get over means to be covering, so the treatment word goes around the next letter

parts.note: aid is help or treatment
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Taking a drug as treatment to recover from a cold.
explanation.definitionFit: LSD is known by this slang name, a hallucinogenic drug.

clue.text: Jumper knitted from rags worn by hippy leader

indicators.note: worn by means the rearranged letters are put on, around, the next letter
knitted suggests strands worked together into a new form, so the letters of the two words are rearranged
leader picks the first letter of the word hippy

explanation.surface: A jumper knitted out of rags is worn by the leader of the hippies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumper' seems to be the knitted sweater; it is the definition, a leaping amphibian. 'From' is fodder, not a link: 'knitted' rearranges it with the rags, and 'worn by' wraps them round H.
explanation.definitionFit: This large amphibian, a leaping animal, is fairly called a jumper.

clue.text: Country putting organ on menu (heart only)

indicators.note: on in an across clue places the organ after the menu letters
heart only keeps just the two central letters of the word menu

parts.note: a gland is an organ of the body

explanation.surface: Putting offal on the menu, but only the heart.
explanation.definitionFit: A nation of the United Kingdom is a country.

clue.text: Having failed, pleased to see passed

indicators.note: having failed suggests something has broken down, so the letters of pleased fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A student who failed is pleased to learn they have passed after all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passed' looks like exam success, set against 'failed'; it means time has gone by.
explanation.definitionFit: Time that has gone by has passed, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Girl — Frenchman going after one

indicators.note: going after puts the Frenchman's name after the one

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
René is a typical French man's name

explanation.surface: A girl, and a Frenchman follows after one.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a female given name, so a girl's name.

clue.text: Boring project with petulant rant?

parts.note: cross means irritable or petulant
to rail is to complain angrily, to rant

explanation.surface: A dull project prompts an irritable tirade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boring' means tunnelling, not dull: this is London's east–west railway, built with huge tunnel-boring machines.
explanation.definitionFit: London's rail line beneath the city was a major tunnelling project, so literally a boring one.
